title: High-throughput microcontact printing of proteins in microwell cell culture plates
author: Chitsaz, Kennedy

steps.title: Fabricate PDMS stamps
steps.instruction: Create thin PDMS squares from a silicone wafer master, cure, cut, and sterilize them for stamping.

substeps.instruction: Tape the silicone wafer master onto the bottom of a 15 cm tissue‑culture dish with Scotch tape, features facing up, sealing the edges; keep the dish closed when not in use and clean the exterior with a nitrogen gun before each use.

Vigorously mix Sylgard 184 elastomer with its curing agent at a 10:1 ratio until a homogeneous frothy mixture forms; pour 22 mL (or an appropriate volume for the well height) into the dish using a dedicated 250 mL beaker and spatula.
Place the dish in a vacuum chamber overnight to remove bubbles and cure the PDMS.
After curing, cut the PDMS slab into square stamps of approximately 1.5–2 cm² that fit into a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Sterilize the stamps by sonication in 70 % ethanol for 5 min; store the stamps in 70 % ethanol at room temperature until needed.

steps.title: Prepare inked circular stamps
steps.instruction: Dry the PDMS squares, cut circular stamps, and load them with fluorescent protein ink in a humidified, light‑protected chamber.

substeps.instruction: In a sterile biosafety cabinet, place the square stamps in an open 15 cm dish and allow any residual ethanol to evaporate completely.
Spray kimwipes with 70 % ethanol, let them dry, then later wet them with dH₂O and keep them in dishes with the stamps to maintain humidity.
Fill two 50 mL Falcon tubes with sterile PBS and sterile dH₂O; keep them within easy reach for rinsing stamps later.
Open the nitrogen tank, wipe the gun nozzle with 70 % ethanol, and keep the gun inside the cabinet for partial drying of stamps.
Plasma‑treat one square coverglass per set of eight stamps for 1 min; record which side was face up (this side will contact the ink).
Plasma‑treat the glass‑bottom 96‑well plate for 1 min.

Using a sterile 5 mm biopsy punch, cut eight circular stamps (≈0.5 cm diameter) from a square PDMS stamp; keep the patterned side facing up and optionally use a magnifying glass to verify orientation.

Prepare 10 µL ink for each circular stamp by mixing the protein of interest (e.g., 50 µg/mL) with a fluorophore‑conjugated antibody to a final concentration of 2 µg/mL in PBS (example: 13 µL of 1 mg/mL PDL + 0.26 µL of 2 mg/mL IgG‑488 diluted to 260 µL total).

Deposit 10 µL of the ink onto each circular stamp, cover with the plasma‑treated coverglass to spread the solution evenly, and incubate for 5 min in a humidified, light‑protected chamber (add a folded sterile kimwipe with 2–3 mL water to the dish corner, close the lid, and cover with aluminum foil).
While the first set inks, prepare the next set of eight stamps (≈3–4 min per set) so stamping can proceed without delay.

steps.title: Pattern wells with inked stamps
steps.instruction: Transfer the inked circular stamps onto the glass‑bottom plate, backfill, and wash the wells.

substeps.instruction: Using sterile forceps, place each inked circular stamp into the biopsy punch so that the inked side faces outward (alternatively, invert the coverglass with stamps still attached; surface tension will hold them).
Dip the loaded punch briefly (~3 s) in PBS, then in dH₂O, and blow‑dry with a low‑pressure nitrogen stream for ~3 s to remove surface droplets without fully drying the ink.

Insert the punch into a well of the plasma‑treated 96‑well plate, press the plunger gently until the stamp contacts the well base, hold the pressure for 5 s, then lift the punch and eject the stamp into waste; the stamp may remain attached in the well temporarily.
Repeat the loading, dipping, and stamping sequence for all remaining wells.

Aspirate any stamps that remain in wells, then add the backfill reference coating solution (e.g., PDL or PEG in PBS) to each well; if no backfill is used, keep the wells filled with PBS to prevent drying of the patterned protein.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for at least 30 min to allow the reference coating to adsorb.
Wash each well three times with 100 µL PBS for 5 min per wash using a multichannel pipette and aspirator.

steps.title: Seed cells, fix, and image
steps.instruction: Culture cells on the patterned plate, fix, optionally stain, and acquire fluorescence images.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a cell suspension in the appropriate culture medium (e.g., neonatal rat oligodendrocytes in SATO media or HEK293 cells in standard medium).
Seed cells at low density: ≤10 000 glial cells per well or 2 500 HEK293 cells per well, adding 200 µL medium to each well of the 96‑well plate.
Incubate cells; patterned substrates remain stable for ≥2 weeks under standard culture conditions.
Remove the culture medium, optionally rinse once with PBS, then add 100 µL of 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS pre‑warmed to 37 °C per well; incubate 10 min at 37 °C.
Wash wells three times with PBS, 5 min each; if imaging is not immediate, store the plate at 4 °C wrapped in parafilm (patterns stable ≥6 months).
Optional: permeabilize cells with 0.05 % Triton X‑100 in PBS for 10 min, then label with fluorescent probes (e.g., Alexa647‑phalloidin) avoiding fluorophores that overlap with the ink label.
Image the wells using an inverted fluorescence microscope capable of viewing the glass‑bottom plate.
Analyze cell morphology, growth, and marker expression on versus off the printed patterns.
